## Dimorphos’s Orbit After DART’s Impact

Before DART’s impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit the larger asteroid Didymos. Immediately afterward, its orbital period was 11 hours, 22 minutes and 37 seconds—32 minutes and 42 seconds shorter.

Over the following weeks, Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, while its orbital period continued to shorten. The period eventually settled at 11 hours, 22 minutes and 3 seconds, a total of 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before the impact. The orbit was also no longer circular after the impact.
